candidate_concepts.label: Extractive summarization selects important sentences directly from the source text
candidate_concepts.description: Extractive summarization works by identifying and concatenating the most salient sentences or spans from the original document. It tends to be grammatically correct and accurate because it reuses existing sentences.

candidate_concepts.label: Abstractive summarization generates paraphrased summaries that may contain new sentences
candidate_concepts.description: Abstractive summarization produces a summary by generating new sentences that paraphrase the source content. It requires deeper semantic understanding and is more challenging than extractive methods, as the model must creatively rephrase information.
coverage_criteria: Explain what abstractive summarization is and how it differs from extractive summarization.
State one reason why abstractive summarization is more difficult (e.g., need for semantic modeling, paraphrase generation).

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video describes abstractive summarization and its challenges at [02:54], emphasizing the need for semantic representation and creative generation.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Distinguishing abstractive from extractive summarization is a key learning point, testable with direct questions.

candidate_concepts.label: BERT can generate sentence embeddings used for clustering in extractive summarization
candidate_concepts.description: Pre-trained BERT models can convert each sentence into a fixed-length vector (e.g., 768 dimensions) that captures semantic meaning. These sentence embeddings are then clustered (e.g., with K-medoids) to select representative sentences for an extractive summary.
coverage_criteria: Explain what a sentence embedding is and how BERT can produce one.
Describe why sentence embeddings are useful for extractive summarization (to group semantically similar sentences).

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video introduces the extractive summarization pipeline at [05:10], explicitly describing how BERT transforms sentences into 768-dimensional vectors.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Sentence embeddings are a core NLP technique; this concept checks understanding of their role in summarization with two focused questions.

candidate_concepts.label: K-medoid clustering selects actual sentences as cluster centers for extractive summaries
candidate_concepts.description: After obtaining sentence embeddings, K-medoid clustering groups similar sentences and uses actual data points (sentences) as cluster medoids. This ensures the extractive summary consists of real sentences from the text, unlike K-Means which can produce virtual centroids.
coverage_criteria: Compare K-Means and K-Medoid, highlighting that K-Medoid uses actual data points as centers.
Explain how K-Medoid can be applied to select representative sentences for a summary.

extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Understanding why and how K-medoid is used for extractive summarization is specific enough to be assessed with a short explanation.

candidate_concepts.label: Keyword extraction from source text guides abstractive summarization models
candidate_concepts.description: In the abstractive summarization approach, important keywords (typically nouns and verbs) are automatically extracted using techniques like NLTK part-of-speech tagging or fine-tuned BERT. These keywords provide a condensed representation of the text’s core topics for the summarization model.

candidate_concepts.label: GPT-2 is fine-tuned for abstractive summarization using a multi-loss training strategy
candidate_concepts.description: The abstractive summarization model uses GPT-2 fine-tuned with two objectives: language modeling (predicting the next token) and multiple-choice prediction (distinguishing true summaries from distractors). The input includes special tokens like `<summarize>` and keywords, and the total loss is a weighted sum (LM:MC = 2:1).

candidate_concepts.label: Masked self-attention in GPT-2 prevents the model from attending to future tokens
candidate_concepts.description: During language modeling, GPT-2 applies a mask to its self-attention mechanism so that each token can only attend to previous tokens (and itself). This auto-regressive property ensures that prediction of the next token is based solely on the preceding context, enabling coherent text generation.
coverage_criteria: Explain what masked self-attention is and why it is necessary for training GPT-2 as a language model.
Describe how the masking works (setting attention weights to -inf before softmax for future positions).

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The video mentions masked self-attention as part of the training strategy intuition at [17:51], noting it blocks information from the right.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Masked self-attention is a fundamental mechanism in transformers; its purpose can be checked with a concise explanation.

candidate_concepts.label: Special tokens like `<summarize>` serve as context cues during GPT-2 fine-tuning
candidate_concepts.description: By inserting a special token such as `<summarize>` between keywords and the summary in the input sequence, the model learns to associate this token with the summarization task. This helps GPT-2 condition its output on the preceding keywords and generate an appropriate summary.
